citation.text: World Bank International Debt Statistics (IDS) (2026), via the Development Finance Observatory

documentation.description: International Debt Statistics (IDS) is the World Bank's annual dataset on the external debt of low- and middle-income countries. It reports debt stocks, disbursements, debt service and projected repayments by borrower and creditor type, with public and publicly guaranteed debt broken down by creditor, from 1970 onwards. The data come mainly from countries' loan-by-loan reporting of public and publicly guaranteed debt to the World Bank's Debtor Reporting System, which is a condition of borrowing from IBRD and IDA.
documentation.attribution: International Debt Statistics by the World Bank, https://datacatalog.worldbank.org/search/dataset/0038015/international-debt-statistics, licensed under CC BY 4.0. Modified by The ONE Campaign.

transformation_log.description: The World Bank publishes IDS as six bulk files, split by debtor name. All six are downloaded each time the pipeline runs, and replace the previous copy, so the data reflects the World Bank's latest release.

transformation_log.transformation: Exclude series outside the debt statistics
transformation_log.description: Non-debt statistics are excluded, including population, balance of payments, investment and reserves. GNI is kept, because some debt ratios are shares of it. Exports of goods, services and primary income, and the three debt ratios that are shares of it, are excluded until the ontology can describe them. Debt forgiveness grants, the stock-flow reconciliation residual, the annual changes in debt stocks and interest arrears, and the present value of debt are also excluded.

transformation_log.transformation: Omit zeros where no lending took place
transformation_log.description: IDS reports a value for every debtor, creditor and series, including pairs with no lending between them, so most figures are zero. Zeros are kept on world totals, and within or after a period of lending between a debtor and a creditor. They are omitted where a creditor has not lent to a debtor, for the years before lending began, and for averages in years with no new commitments, since there is nothing to average.

Debtor and creditor codes are standardised to Data Commons IDs used across the platform, so data can be compared across datasets. Where a series names a single lender in its code, such as debt owed to the IBRD, that lender becomes the creditor.

Every figure is reported against the year, the debtor and the creditor, and the dimensions the World Bank encodes in each series code, such as type of flow, maturity and creditor type. GNI is the exception: it describes the debtor economy, so it is reported against the year and the economy alone. Ratios record what they are a share of: GNI or total external debt stocks. Every amount is reported in US dollars at current prices.

For the years after the last reported year, the World Bank projects debt service and disbursements on commitments already made. These values are marked as estimated, so they are kept apart from reported values.

changes.note: External debt stocks, flows and debt service of low- and middle-income countries by borrower and creditor, with related ratios and gross national income.

documentation.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
documentation.description: DAC2A is the OECD Development Assistance Committee's table of ODA disbursements by donor and recipient country or region. It covers bilateral donors and multilateral agencies reporting their own outflows, and includes the OECD's estimate of each donor's core multilateral contributions attributed to recipients.
documentation.attribution: OECD (2026), OECD DAC2A, OECD Data Explorer, https://webfs-dcd.oecd.org/files/dotStat/DSD_DAC2/Table2a_Data.zip (accessed on 2026-10-12)

transformation_log.description: The OECD publishes DAC2A in April, June, September and December. The complete table is downloaded from the OECD each time it is republished, and replaces the previous copy, so the data reflects the OECD's latest release.

Before each full release, the OECD publishes preliminary data for the year that release covers, as reporters submit it. Until then, that year is partial, so the pipeline excludes it. Support for partial years is in development. Partial years will be marked incomplete, so they don't lead to incorrect or confusing analyses.

Provider and recipient codes are standardised to Data Commons IDs used across the platform, so data can be compared across datasets. The totals DAC2A reports for groups of providers, such as all DAC countries, and for groups of recipients, such as regions and income groups, are included as providers and recipients of their own. Where two provider codes name the same organisation and report the same figures, the figures are counted once. Where two recipient codes name the same organisation, such as IDA and IDA's Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative, their flows are added.

Only figures in current US dollars are included, not constant US dollars. Only flows to recipients on Part I of the DAC List are included: the developing countries, and the multilateral organisations DAC2A reports as recipients, such as development banks and UN agencies. Flows to Part II recipients, the countries in transition, are excluded.
DAC2A reports amounts in millions, which are converted to whole units. ODA per person and ODA as a share of GNI are kept as reported.

Each figure is reported by year, provider, recipient and type of aid, such as grants, repayments, interest received, or debt forgiven or rescheduled. DAC2A is a table of disbursements, so every figure, repayments and interest included, is recorded as a disbursement. Figures are marked as gross or net, except where DAC2A does not say which, and as grants or non-grants where the type of aid is wholly one or the other. Imputed multilateral ODA, the OECD's estimate of each provider's share of multilateral organisations' ODA, is marked as modelled. ODA as a share of GNI records the recipient's GNI as its denominator, and ODA per person records the recipient's population.

changes.note: The partial preliminary year published ahead of the next full release is excluded.
ODA disbursements by donor and recipient country or region, including the OECD's imputed multilateral contributions, and ODA per person and as a share of recipient GNI.
